iut_type: Subset creation (reduced-profile-support derivative design) remains possible post-2024, but with increased rejection risk under strengthened Consistency Check -- Profile/Service removal subsets succeed more often than other reduction types
customer_question: Is it still possible, as before, to create a Subset of a registered design with reduced supported profiles, and then register derivative models linked to that Subset?
question_variants: Has the success rate of creating a Subset changed under the post-2024 registration system?
Is there a type of Subset reduction that's more likely to succeed than others?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to know whether the previously-available strategy of defining a Subset (a derivative design with reduced supported profiles relative to the original registered design) and registering derivative models against that Subset remained a viable option under the post-2024 registration system.
plain_english_explanation: Defining a Subset and registering derivative models linked to it remains possible as a system feature -- this capability itself was not removed by the 2024 overhaul. However, the underlying Controller-Host inter-layer consistency checking was strengthened starting July 1, 2024. The old system also required passing Consistency Check (achieving No Invalid) during Subset definition, but the new system's Consistency Check is now considerably more stringent, meaning the probability of a Subset-creation attempt being rejected has increased compared to before. Based on practical experience, Subsets that simply remove a BLE Profile or Service from the supported set tend to have a relatively higher success rate than other kinds of reduction -- implying that more granular layer-level reductions (such as removing specific Core-layer or PHY-mode support) are more likely to trigger Consistency Check failures than dropping an entire Profile or Service wholesale.
consultant_answer: Yes, defining a Subset and registering derivative models against it remains possible -- that capability wasn't removed. But the underlying Consistency Check has been strengthened since July 2024, so the probability of a Subset-creation attempt being rejected has gone up compared to before. From experience, Subsets that simply remove a BLE Profile or Service tend to succeed more often than other types of reduction.
decision_logic: When a customer wants to create a Subset with reduced profile/feature support, confirm the capability remains available but set expectations that rejection risk has increased under the strengthened post-2024 Consistency Check, and favor Profile/Service-level removals over other reduction types when designing the Subset, since these have a historically higher success rate.
final_recommendation: When scoping a Subset-creation strategy for a customer, proactively explain the increased rejection risk under the current Consistency Check regime and recommend structuring the reduction as a Profile/Service removal where possible, rather than letting the customer discover the increased difficulty only after an attempt fails.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer attempting a Subset reduction at a finer granularity than Profile/Service removal (e.g., removing specific Core-layer features) without anticipating the higher rejection risk could waste time on a Subset-creation attempt that the strengthened Consistency Check is more likely to reject.
